newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on soy rally, farm selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on soy rally, farm selling.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a late short covering rally that started in the soy complex with slow farmer selling also mentioned, traders said.

"We got down to a value area and farmers are not selling. We're waiting for the January report (USDA final 1996 crop report) and we'll go from there," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Corn dropped early in response to a bearish corn export number in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended November 28 were at 242,800 tonnes.
That tally was well below trade expectations for 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
The new low for March corn was $2.60-1/2 per bushel down from the previous low of $2.62-1/4 which was set Tuesday.
Traders also cited commercial bear spreading.
ADM Investor Services bear spread six million bushels of March/December at 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel, premium December, the traders said.
Corn closed unchanged to 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up 2-1/2 at $2.68-1/2. March closed up 3-3/4 cents at $2.67.

Key players included Cargill Inc with purchases of three million bushels of March and a sale of three million May, traders said. The Chicago Corp sold three million March and Refco Inc bought and sold three million March, they said.
The market was underpinned early, remained resiliant and was showing a propensity for a short covering bounce.

The short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December dropped to 38 points at midsession, down from the recent high of 61 set on the close November 25. An RSI of 70 or more is considered indicative of an overbought market and 30 or less as oversold.

Chartists cited first support in the December at $2.65 and second support at $2.63. The session low for December was $2.64. First resistance in December was $2.67 and second resistance at $2.69. The session high was $2.69-1/2.
Technicians reported longer term key moving averages as bearish for corn futures.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, above the 57,314 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, LIT America sold 500 March $2.70 calls at five cents, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 800 July $3.00 calls and sold 800 July $2.50 puts at 11-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 16,169 traded Wednesday.
